/-! # The least dimension-independent complex coordinate Hlawka constant

This packages admissibility and the three-coordinate cyclic obstruction into
one statement, with an explicit lower cutoff on the real exponent.
-/

open HlawkaSchatten
open HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalConstruction
formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalConstruction.campaign_cutoff21 :
    ∀ p : ℝ, 21 ≤ p →
      IsLeast {C : ℝ | ∀ n : ℕ,
        HasHlawkaConstant (lpNorm p : (Fin n → ℂ) → ℝ) C}
        (cyclicConstant p) := by sorry
theorem_title: The least uniform complex coordinate Hlawka constant for p ≥ 21
natural_language_statement:
For every real exponent p ≥ 21, let N_p(x) be the foundation's finite coordinate p-norm and let K_p be its unchanged cyclicConstant p, defined as the supremum of the cyclic ratio over t ∈ [1/2, 2].

Then K_p is the least real constant C such that the triple deficit N_p(x) + N_p(y) + N_p(z) − N_p(x + y + z) is at most C times the pair-deficit sum 2(N_p(x) + N_p(y) + N_p(z)) − N_p(x + y) − N_p(x + z) − N_p(y + z), for every natural-number dimension n and all complex vectors x, y, z in that dimension.

This combines admissibility and optimality uniformly over all finite complex coordinate dimensions. It includes dimension zero and arbitrary triples with unequal or zero norms. The same shared definitions are used throughout; the claim concerns complex diagonal matrices via their coordinate norms.
source: Yuxuan Xu (徐宇轩), School of Computer Science, Wuhan University. A computer-assisted sharp diagonal Hlawka inequality for real exponents p >= 21, v1, 17 October 2026. https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/2f1ec21c8ce4e3d9de33f57119f73f8504de0bd3/paper/main.pdf . LaTeX: https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/2f1ec21c8ce4e3d9de33f57119f73f8504de0bd3/paper/main.tex . Reproducibility: https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/2f1ec21c8ce4e3d9de33f57119f73f8504de0bd3/results/release-replay.json . AI-assisted research preprint; independent analytic review pending; no new Lean proof. Main Theorem 1.1. The campaign template is preserved, changing only its declaration name and numeric cutoff.
readback: For every real number $p\ge 21$, let $N_{p,n}(x)=\bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}|x_i|^p\bigr)^{1/p}$ for each natural number $n$ and each vector $x\in\mathbb C^n$, where $|x_i|$ is the complex modulus, and define $A_p(t)=(t^p+2)^{1/p}$, $B_p(t)=(2|1-t|^p+2^p)^{1/p}$, and $K_p=\sup\bigl\{\frac{3A_p(t)-3^{1/p}|2-t|}{6A_p(t)-3B_p(t)}:t\in[\tfrac12,2]\bigr\}$. Then $K_p$ is the least real number $C$ such that, for every natural number $n$ and all $x,y,z\in\mathbb C^n$, $N_{p,n}(x)+N_{p,n}(y)+N_{p,n}(z)-N_{p,n}(x+y+z)\le C\bigl[(N_{p,n}(x)+N_{p,n}(y)-N_{p,n}(x+y))+(N_{p,n}(x)+N_{p,n}(z)-N_{p,n}(x+z))+(N_{p,n}(y)+N_{p,n}(z)-N_{p,n}(y+z))\bigr]$. Explicitly, this inequality holds with $C=K_p$ simultaneously for every such dimension and triple, and $K_p\le C$ for every real $C$ for which it holds simultaneously for every dimension and triple; the competing constants $C$ have no separately imposed sign restriction. The quantifiers include zero vectors and $n=0$: in dimension zero the coordinate sum is empty, $N_{p,0}=0$, and the required inequality is $0\le 0$ for every real $C$.

theorem_title: Scalar bounds on the full real window [21, 26]
formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalCutoff21.scalar_window21 :
    ∀ p : ℝ, 21 ≤ p → p ≤ 26 →
      (273 / 625 : ℝ) * p < cyclicConstant p ∧
      cyclicConstant p ≤ p / 2 ∧
      scalarEnvelope p (1011 / 2500 : ℝ) < cyclicConstant p := by sorry

readback:
For every real number $p$ with $21\le p\le26$ (including both endpoints), let $C(p)$ be the real supremum
$$C(p)=\sup\left\{\frac{3(t^p+2)^{1/p}-3^{1/p}|2-t|}{6(t^p+2)^{1/p}-3\bigl(2|1-t|^p+2^p\bigr)^{1/p}}:\ t\in\mathbb R,\ \frac12\le t\le2\right\}.$$
Then all three inequalities hold simultaneously:
$$\frac{273}{625}p<C(p),\qquad C(p)\le\frac p2,\qquad \frac{1-\frac{1011}{2500}}{2\left(1-\left(\frac{1+(\frac{1011}{2500})^p}{2}\right)^{1/p}\right)}<C(p).$$
Here every power is a real power, $|\cdot|$ is the absolute value on $\mathbb R$, and division has the total real-number convention $a/0=0$.

readback: For every real number $p$ with $21\le p\le26$, define $N_p(v)=(|v_0|^p+|v_1|^p+|v_2|^p)^{1/p}$ for every real coordinate triple $v=(v_0,v_1,v_2)\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $C_p$ be the real supremum of the set $\left\{\dfrac{3(t^p+2)^{1/p}-3^{1/p}|2-t|}{6(t^p+2)^{1/p}-3\bigl(2|1-t|^p+2^p\bigr)^{1/p}}:\ t\in\mathbb R,\ \tfrac12\le t\le2\right\}$, with real powers and real division (division by zero, if encountered, has value zero). Then for every three real coordinate triples $x,y,z\in\mathbb R^3$, with addition performed coordinatewise, $N_p(x)+N_p(y)+N_p(z)-N_p(x+y+z)\le C_p\bigl((N_p(x)+N_p(y)-N_p(x+y))+(N_p(x)+N_p(z)-N_p(x+z))+(N_p(y)+N_p(z)-N_p(y+z))\bigr)$. There is no assumption that any of $x,y,z$ is nonzero or that their values under $N_p$ are equal: the assertion includes arbitrary unequal values, cancellation in any pair or in the total sum, and every zero-input case; if, for example, $z=0$, it states $N_p(x)+N_p(y)-N_p(x+y)\le C_p(N_p(x)+N_p(y)-N_p(x+y))$, with the analogous statements when either other input is zero, while if at least two inputs are zero both sides are zero.
